title: Per-tenant "safety cage" with progressive trip curves, warm-backoff, and deterministic fallback allocator
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Design and implement a per-tenant "safety cage" (tenant-level attenuation) that detects harmful dependency/model/tenant degradations and applies progressive trip curves, warm-backoff, and deterministic fallback routing. This ticket covers metric definition, threshold calibration, runtime interceptor implementation, safe fallback decision logic (region-aware, model-variant aware), rollout plan, and monitoring/alerting tuned to SLO impact. The aim is to preserve global SLOs while minimizing customer-visible failures and avoiding feedback amplification across tenants.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-tenant breaker state (OPEN/HALF_OPEN/CLOSED) and a deterministic fallback route for each trip event
Trip decision uses configured composite signal (error rate, p95 latency, queue growth) and supports quantile-window calibration per tenant tier
Warm-backoff ramp-down is implemented: a tenant in half-open is allowed controlled qps increase based on exponential step with success checks
Fallback allocator follows deterministic policy: prefer same-region compatible model variant -> dedicated pool -> hosted fallback pool, and records decision traces to console
Simulated chaos tests show <1% additional SLO violations compared to baseline across modeled outages, and no cascading model pool exhaustion
Dashboard shows per-tenant histograms, trip counts, and SLO-credit consumed; alerts fire when tenant trips cause >5% SLO degradation over 5m window
implementation_plan: Design metric window: 60s sliding window for error-rate with 10s subwindows + 5m moving p95 latency quantile via t-digest approximation
Trip function: composite_score = w1*error_rate_norm + w2*latency_p95_norm + w3*queue_growth_norm; trip when composite_score > tenant_threshold; tenant_threshold defaults selected by tier (P0/P1/P2)
State machine: CLOSED -> OPEN (immediate trip) -> HALF_OPEN (after backoff TTL) -> CLOSED on sustained success. HALF_OPEN uses token-bucket allowance with exponential warm-backoff steps

Fallback allocator module: deterministic priority list for fallbacks per tenant configured in runtime config service (region-pref, model-variant compatibility matrix, cost cap). Fallback decisions emitted as event with route_id and reason

Runtime changes: add BreakerInterceptor in inference-gateway; metric collectors (ring buffer) per tenant; decision evaluation runs in hot path with bounded CPU (<0.5% extra p99 latency) using cached t-digest summaries
Config API: admin and tenant override endpoints; allow emergency global soft-trip knob to force-protect critical pools
Testing: unit tests for trip function math, integration tests with staged model pool failures, large-scale synthetic load test in staging with 10k RPS and 1% injected dependency errors
PRs: gateway interceptor + metrics (#github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6213), config schema + migration (#github.com/redwood-inference/config/pull/204)
Docs: Confluence design doc + diagrams (link below) and runbook entries for operator-led manual rollback
monitoring_and_alerting: Per-tenant trip_count and trip_rate (1m/5m) metrics exported to metric-store
SLO impact metric: tenant_contribution_to_slo_violation (5m window). Alert if any tenant contributes >5% of violations for 5m
Pool pressure alert: when fallback allocator routes >X% traffic to a fallback pool for >10m, trigger capacity/ops paging
Anomaly detection: sudden jump in trip_rate without corresponding error-rate increase triggers investigation playbook
Tracing: every fallback decision adds tags: fallback.reason, fallback.target, fallback.prev_state; sampled traces surfaced in Console
migration_and_rollout: Phase 0 - dry-run in staging: enable interceptor but only log decisions for 48h. Run synthetic failure scenarios and collect traces
Phase 1 - canary: enable for 5 low-traffic tenants in us-west with soft-trip (trip only logged, not enforced) for 72h
Phase 2 - enforced canary: enforce for same 5 tenants with conservative thresholds and 1% probabilistic fallback to test routing under real traffic
Phase 3 - regional rollout: enable in us-west for 50 tenants, monitor SLO impact for 7d, increase tenant pool and adjust thresholds
Phase 4 - global: enable by default with tenant tiers; enable emergency global kill-switch and auto rollback if SLO degradation >2% vs baseline
Rollback plan: scale down enforcement to logging-only and revert config via runtime config API; run post-mortem if rollback occurs
dependencies: ENG-82377 (service-registry: stable region-tagging + health TTL) - required for region-aware fallbacks
MON-902 (metric-ingest: new per-tenant high-card metrics retention)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives for noisy tenants cause unnecessary fallback => Mitigation: require composite_score sustained for 3 contiguous subwindows before open
Risk: fallback pools could be overloaded by deterministic routing => Mitigation: allocator includes admission checks and local soft-circuit on target pool, plus proportional shedding
Risk: metric cardinality explosion from per-tenant state => Mitigation: aggregate over tenant cohorts by default and only enable high-card metrics for tenants flagged by ops
Risk: cross-region routing increases latency for latency-sensitive tenants => Mitigation: region-pref policy enforces max added RTT budget (default 50ms), otherwise prefer local degrade
Risk: miscalibrated warm-backoff causes oscillation => Mitigation: include hysteresis and exponential backoff with max backoff cap and bootstrapping grace period
comments: 2025-11-03 - Sofia Patel: Initial design readout posted. Requesting feedback from SRE and runtime teams on metric choices and p95 window size.
2025-11-05 - Marco Nguyen (SRE): Prefer using 5m quantile with a 1m guard to avoid transient p95 spikes. Concern about cardinality; suggest cohort fallbacks.
2025-11-07 - Priya Kapoor (Product): Please ensure fallback behavior is transparent to customers. Add tracing and cost estimates per fallback decision.
2025-11-10 - Ethan Morales: Implemented prototype interceptor and t-digest summaries. Local staging tests show p99 extra latency < 3ms. Opened PR #6213.
2025-11-14 - Design review comment (Aisha Romero): UX for Console needs clear visualization of tenant trips and deterministic fallback chain; added mockups to Confluence

2025-11-16 - Load test result (Ethan): Synthetic 10k RPS test with 1% injected model failures. Breaker engaged for noisy tenants and routed ~0.8% of total traffic to fallback pools. Measured SLO impact: +0.6% violations vs baseline; within acceptance criteria
